passageLocation.openingWords: As I put on pace, night

text: As I put on pace, night followed day like the flapping of a black wing. The dim suggestion of the laboratory seemed presently to fall away from me, and I saw the sun hopping swiftly across the sky, leaping it every minute, and every minute marking a day. I supposed the laboratory had been destroyed and I had come into the open air. I had a dim impression of scaffolding, but I was already going too fast to be conscious of any moving things. The slowest snail that ever crawled dashed by too fast for me.

curation.context: In Chapter IV of Wells’s 1895 novel, the Time Traveller describes accelerating beyond the ordinary rhythm of days and nights.
curation.rationale: Black wings, a hopping sun, racing days, open air, scaffolding and an impossibly fast snail make time tangible. The verbs and reversals offer unusually playful selection paths.
